title: TokenClaims
description: Claims carried in the signed runtime lease token. Source of truth: DSL Best Practices Chapter 11.05 and Annex C. Standard JWT claims (RFC 7519) combined with DSL-specific claims.

iss.description: Issuer identifier of the control plane. Spec (Annex C) uses a URL, e.g. https://lic.example.com. NOTE (delta D10): the implementation currently emits the opaque string 'dsl-control-plane'; the spec (URL) is authoritative.

sub.description: Subject of the grant = the bound workload identity. NOTE (delta D10, high priority): the implementation currently sets 'sub' to tenantId; the spec (bound workload) is authoritative and tenant is carried separately in tenantId. This changes token validation logic.

aud.description: Intended application/service audience (the app the token was issued for).

iat.description: Issued-at time (NumericDate, seconds since epoch per RFC 7519).

app.description: Licensed application identifier. NOTE (delta D2): 'app' vs 'appId' to be confirmed; the implementation token claim is 'appId'.

dimensions.description: Granted dimension values for local enforcement.

boundIdentity.description: Binding summary needed for local validation semantics.

$comment: additionalProperties is true because vendor-specific claims MAY be added (Chapter 11.05), but they MUST NOT alter canonical claim meaning. RFC 7519 date claims are integers (NumericDate); note the spec's Annex C prose shows ISO-8601 strings for readability - implementations should use NumericDate integers per RFC 7519. Flagged as a minor spec editorial clarification.
